title: Greg Pruitt: Two-Time All-American and 1972 Heisman Runner-Up
question: Where did Greg Pruitt finish in the Heisman voting at Oklahoma?
answer: Greg Pruitt (OU 1970-72) finished third in the 1971 Heisman Trophy voting and second in 1972. He was a unanimous All-American both seasons.
summary: Greg Pruitt finished third in 1971 and second in 1972 Heisman voting as a two-time unanimous All-American halfback, averaging 7.6 yards a carry at OU.
body: Greg Pruitt (OU 1970-72) was a speedy halfback who made Oklahoma's wishbone offense look like a track meet. He played three seasons for the Sooners and left a trail of highlights that still show up on any list of the program's great runners.

His junior year of 1971 was his breakout. The College Football Hall of Fame notes that he averaged 9.4 yards per rushing play that season, and the Sooners' ground game rolled to a national runner-up finish. When the Heisman votes were counted he placed third, and he was named a unanimous All-American.

He came back in 1972 and did it again. Pruitt earned unanimous All-America honors for a second straight year and finished second in the Heisman Trophy balloting, a step higher than the year before. He also earned first-team All-Big Eight recognition in both of his last two seasons.

Across his Oklahoma career he carried the ball 375 times and averaged 7.6 yards per carry, according to the Hall of Fame. Add in his work in bowl games, including the Sugar Bowl wins that closed the 1971 and 1972 seasons, and it is easy to see why he was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1999. Fans who want the rest of the story can read about his pro career with the Browns and Raiders in our earlier post.
